fields: Do Not Start With This When

rows.Key Difference: Detects molecular regions from spatial-expression structure before low-rank imputation, making region context explicit rather than relying on image features or deep generative models.
rows.Evidence Note: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Communications method paper and the paper reports official code availability. Comparator and scale labels are Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When Visium-like spot data need region-aware imputation with interpretable molecular regions.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When matched image signal or scRNA reference dependence is the main requirement or when imputed expression values should be avoided.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Region-level low-rank imputation can smooth boundaries or rare-cell signals if detected regions are heterogeneous.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: denoising through spatially informed gene filtering
rows.Main Output: filtered gene set / denoised feature matrix
rows.Key Difference: Filters noisy genes rather than imputing expression values, making it a boundary method between denoising and feature selection.
rows.Evidence Note: PubMed/DOI verify the Cell Systems method paper and the current Layer 1 registry already records the official GitHub link. Its placement is a deliberate Layer 2 boundary decision.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the main need is conservative noise-gene filtering before downstream analysis without filling missing counts.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the goal is missing-gene imputation, matrix enhancement, or preserving every measured feature.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Filtering can discard broad but real biological signals; this row overlaps Normalization / Feature Selection.

rows.Main Input: ST matrix + spatial coordinates + image or pseudo-image signal
rows.Key Difference: Uses location and image-derived or pseudo-image structure for denoising rather than region-only or scRNA-reference-assisted imputation.
rows.Evidence Note: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Methods method paper and the paper reports official GitHub code. Image-use and scale labels combine direct method description with Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When spatial position and histology or pseudo-image structure are expected to help recover expression signal.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When no reliable image or spatial-position signal should influence denoising.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Image or pseudo-image graph construction can import morphology bias and over-smooth small structures.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: deep generative enhancement and denoising for ST quality improvement
rows.Key Difference: Uses graph/deep generative diffusion modeling for stronger enhancement rather than conservative filtering or explicit scRNA-reference imputation.
rows.Evidence Note: PubMed/DOI verify the Briefings in Bioinformatics method paper and the article reports source code. Benchmark claims are method-paper-local rather than an independent all-method ranking.
rows.Best First Choice When: When GPU/deep generative enhancement is acceptable and downstream spatial-domain-quality improvement is also relevant.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When CPU-only conservative denoising or count-preserving preprocessing is the first-order requirement.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Generative enhancement can amplify or hallucinate structure optimized for downstream clustering.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: scRNA-reference-assisted imputation of missing ST genes
rows.Key Difference: Uses single-cell transcriptomics as an external reference, unlike reference-free spatial or image-informed methods.
rows.Evidence Note: PubMed/DOI verify the Briefings in Bioinformatics method paper and the article reports official code availability. Reference-dependence is directly supported; risk caveat is Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When a high-quality tissue-matched scRNA-seq reference is available and missing-gene imputation is the main goal.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When no suitable scRNA-seq reference exists or reference mismatch is a primary concern.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Reference mismatch or batch differences can propagate scRNA-seq priors into spatial imputation.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: graph contrastive denoising and imputation coupled to spatial-domain representation
rows.Key Difference: Jointly targets domain identification, denoising, and imputation through multi-task graph contrastive representation learning.
rows.Evidence Note: PubMed/DOI verify the BMC Biology method paper and the paper reports official GitHub and Zenodo sources. Multi-task role is direct; comparator caveats are Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When denoising/imputation should be coupled with graph representation and spatial-domain discovery.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When preprocessing should remain clearly separated from clustering/domain assumptions.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: The multi-task objective can entangle denoising with domain-calling assumptions and needs independent downstream sanity checks.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: reference-free denoising and imputation with pretrained model priors
rows.Key Difference: Uses genomic-language-model priors without requiring scRNA-seq reference, making it a model-prior-assisted reference-free route.
rows.Evidence Note: PubMed/DOI verify the Genome Research method paper, which is an update of a preprint, and the full text reports GitHub code plus high memory/GPU resource use. Model-prior risk is Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When reference-free imputation is needed and a strong pretrained gene-prior route plus high compute burden is acceptable.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When low-resource CPU-first analysis or avoidance of foundation-model prior effects is required.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Genomic-language-model priors may produce plausible but unvalidated expression and require careful biological sanity checks.
